narrative: Investors should watch whether ASML’s order intake and outlook show that AI-related semiconductor demand is translating into sustained equipment spending, especially after Samsung’s Q3 guidance indicated that AI demand is outstripping memory supply. The call will also be important for clues from major customers such as TSMC, Samsung, and SK Hynix, as well as for any discussion of delivery timing and demand for ASML’s most advanced lithography systems. Given the broader earnings-season and Fed-focused headlines, management’s comments on macroeconomic uncertainty, customer capital-expenditure plans, and export restrictions—particularly concerning China—may matter as much as the quarter itself. My expectation is cautiously constructive if ASML confirms strong AI-driven demand and a healthy backlog, but investors may react negatively if shipments, orders, or guidance are constrained by customer timing, supply-chain issues, or geopolitical limits.

guidance_summary: Q4 2026 revenue guided to €14.2-15.2 billion with approximately 57% gross margin, €3.7 billion of installed-base-management sales, €1.2 billion of R&D and €0.4 billion of SG&A. FY2026 revenue guided to €44-45 billion, up approximately 36% year over year, with approximately 56% gross margin; EUV growth is expected above 45%, non-EUV systems around 20%, and installed-base management around 50%. Memory system sales are expected to grow 75%, logic 10% and advanced logic above 25%. Management is targeting 30% capacity growth in 2027 for low-NA EUV and DUV immersion and is investigating capacity growth above 30% in 2028; no hard capex guidance was provided.
key_qa_moments: Analysts pressed management on whether ASML could materially exceed the 30% capacity-growth plan, including whether 140-150 EUV systems could be produced in 2028. Management declined to provide new 2027/2028 unit targets but cited factory-footprint optimization, shorter cycle times and supplier expansion as meaningful levers.

Analysts questioned whether customer forecasts for 2029-2030 reflected speculative slot-reservation behavior. Management said purchase orders require substantial, painful down payments and real commitments, while ASML is deliberately delaying acceptance of later-year orders until it can balance total demand and capacity fairly across customers.

On pricing, management was unusually specific that increases have been completed for the most critical, high-volume-manufacturing products and associated upgrades, with some benefit in 2027 and the full impact from 2028 onward, while declining to disclose exact products or backlog treatment.

On gross margin, management explained that Q4 margin is expected to decline sequentially despite higher revenue because ramp costs will offset fixed-cost absorption. It also highlighted upgrade demand as a major swing factor for margins beyond 2026.
risks: Capacity expansion may be constrained by ramp costs, supply-chain execution and the need to support suppliers as output rises above 30% annually.

Customer cleanroom and fab-construction execution could create tactical installation delays in 2027-2028 even though management does not view cleanroom availability as a major current demand constraint.
Installed-base upgrade revenue and its exceptionally high margins may not be fully sustainable, making upgrades a key swing factor for future gross margin.
Management would not quantify 2027 or 2028 output, leaving uncertainty around the ability to satisfy demand implied by customer interest in 2029-2030.
High-NA EUV adoption is progressing, but the timing and scale of the production ramp remain uncertain; customer capacity build-outs could either accelerate or delay adoption.

China represents approximately 20% of FY2026 sales, creating continuing exposure to export controls and future market-access risk, despite management's confidence in local demand and competitive positioning.
summary: The call was strongly bullish on demand, with record Q3 results, raised FY2026 revenue expectations and customer visibility extending through 2028 and into 2029-2030. Q&A reinforced the long thesis through evidence of real customer commitments, broad logic and memory demand, pricing increases and multiple capacity-expansion levers, although ramp costs, upgrade mix and execution constraints temper near-term margin upside.
